answer: Stake-locked identity defeats Sybil attacks: each agent locks collateral in a vault, slashed if it signs conflicting attestations for one task. Reward weight grows with the square root of stake, so splitting funds across fake identities earns less than one honest agent, yet each identity still needs full collateral. The zenith of influence requires aged, attested stake, not minted accounts. An attacker must front the nectar of real capital for every forged persona, so doubling fake identities roughly quadruples locked cost while halving per-identity return.
